paragraphs: Here's the big idea, friend. When you're worn out from living around people who twist words and want a fight, you don't have to carry it alone. This writer did the most important thing first: "In my distress I cried to the LORD, and He answered me." (Psalm 120:1) That's where the song starts, and I think that's where your hard days can start too.

The writer doesn't pretend the trouble is small. The prayer is for deliverance from "lying lips and a deceitful tongue." (Psalm 120:2) Then comes the ache: "Too long have I dwelt among those who hate peace." (Psalm 120:6) Baker, God's people are allowed to say that out loud. Honest words about a hard place are part of the prayer.

And look at the last line: "I am in favor of peace; but when I speak, they want war." (Psalm 120:7) The writer wants peace, and that wanting is real even when the people around don't want it. So if you're stuck in a place where peace is not what everybody is chasing, bring it to the LORD like this writer did. He's the One who answered, and He's the One you can cry to first.
